assessment: The supplied slips show preparation confusion and uneven reported practice, but do not establish their causes or represent every attendance. Pair formation and prior familiarity are plausible intervention points. Both openings are hypotheses requiring six-session outcome and workload checks.

openings.claim: Give every conversation a fresh information gap: each participant privately chooses an unseen prompt or personal example, then partners alternate explaining and asking. Offer optional printed sentence starters and deeper follow-up questions without proficiency labels. Begin with adjacent seats and permit partner changes.
openings.delta: A frequent attendee's familiarity becomes less decisive because neither partner knows the other's chosen content. Prompt support replaces public level assignment, while immediate seating reduces the initial matching decision.
openings.prediction: Compared with ordinary shared-sheet rounds, occasional attendees will report easier entry and more useful speaking, and observers will record shorter pairing delays and less unequal speaking time.
openings.probe: Counterbalance ordinary and fresh-gap rounds within sessions using existing sheets. Observe pairing delay and individual speaking duration anonymously; collect round-specific usefulness and entry-difficulty slips with optional attendance-frequency categories. Include accessible triad turn-taking when numbers are odd.
assumptions: Unknown partner content can create conversational interest at differing levels.
Participants can choose helpful support privately.
Printing and setup fit the weekly coordination budget.

openings.claim: Use a stable preparation invitation across weeks: choose one recent experience, object, or question to discuss. Put it on a reusable printed card, with optional weekly-topic examples. Reserve a session opening exchange for whatever participants brought or recalled; offer an immediate example to anyone arriving unprepared.
openings.delta: Preparation attaches to the participant's next attendance rather than a sequence of weekly assignments, potentially removing the earlier-task trap without penalizing absences.
openings.prediction: Task identification improves particularly among occasional attendees, preparation questions consume less volunteer time, and prepared material supports useful conversation.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, ask participants to describe their next preparation action and anonymously record whether their material supported useful speaking. Track all attendees, missing responses, and volunteer minutes by activity; assess the original three success thresholds together.
assumptions: A recurring invitation remains motivating and sufficiently clear.
Personal material can support conversation at participants' current levels.
Cards and reminders can be provided within existing resources.
